articles.title: Walsh settles for bronze with semi-final defeat
articles.summary: Michaela Walsh will return from the European Boxing Championships in Bulgaria with a bronze medal as she loses out in her featherweight semi-final.
body: The 33-year-old Belfast woman lost on a 4-1 split decision by Kazakhstan-born Hungarian Vladislava Kukhta [29-28, 29-28, 29-28, 29-28, 28-29] after a technical bout of contrasting styles.
Walsh has now secured three podium finishes this year following silver medals at the Commonwealth Games and Strandja Tournament.

"It was very cagey and the tactics were to try and lead her on [into counters] but she is a great operator and it was always just how that first round was going to go as it would dictate the fight," Walsh reflected when speaking to Boxing Ireland.

"2023 was the last time I was on an international podium [until this year]. I was going through a bit of a stale period, but never gave up, believed in myself and knew I could produce big performances.

articles.title: Sandro Mazzola obituary
articles.summary: Outstanding footballer who won two European Cups with Internazionale and a World Cup runners-up medal with Italy. The Italian footballer Sandro Mazzola, who has died aged 83, was a supremely gifted forward who won two European Cups and four Serie A titles during 17 years with his only club…
body: He was six years old when his father, Valentino Mazzola, the captain of an invincible Torino team and of Italy, died aged 30, along with the rest of the team, when their chartered plane, returning in bad weather from a friendly fixture in Lisbon in May 1949, crashed into the Superga hill overlooking Turin, killing everyone on board. The demise of Il Grande Torino, as they were known, traumatized the nation.

When Sandro emerged from that tragedy to win his first European Cup in 1964, defeating the five-times champions Real Madrid 3-1 in the final, he scored two of Internazionale’s goals. In a recent interview he recalled that afterwards the veteran Argentinian forward Alfredo Di Stefano, the greatest of Madrid’s stars, gave him his shirt while telling him: “You are worthy of your father.”

articles.title: Vinícius Júnior et al land in unlikely outpost of Townsville as Brazil reboot begins | Joey Lynch
articles.summary: The Seleção’s rebuild after their latest World Cup exit begins against the Socceroos in a place better known for rugby league than joga bonito. It’s a safe bet that Vinícius Júnior, who plays week in and week out for Real Madrid at the Santiago Bernabéu, doesn’t know about North Queensland Fury.
body: Maybe in the spirit of cultural exchange, then, Raphinha will be posting #BringBackTheFury on his Instagram page by the time the Seleção departs the Sunshine State next week. Such a post would only feel slightly more surreal than the Barcelona attacker rubbing shoulders at Townsville airport with almost 80 junior rugby league sides from around Queensland, jetting in for the Gordon Tallis Cup.

Nor would it feel more incongruous than Carlo Ancelotti beginning his first full World Cup cycle as Brazil boss by staying a 10-minute walk from the Mad Cow Tavern on Flinders Street, preparing for games in Townsville and Brisbane against a Socceroos side led by Tony Popovic who, once upon a time, served as his guest as both AC Milan and Bayern Munich.

“We are good friends,” Ancelotti said. “Sometimes we have the possibility to meet to talk about football. We spent time together when I was in Milan, we spent time together in Brisbane two nights ago. It’s a pleasure to talk about football [with Popovic]. He’s doing a fantastic job here. A really passionate manager. I hope the best for him. I think the World Cup he had was a really good World Cup. The team showed strong quality, a compact team.”

articles.title: Chadwick joins elite group of British women to drive F1 car after test
articles.summary: Jamie Chadwick has joined an elite group of British women to drive a Formula One car after she took part in a test for Williams - a day the 28-year-old hailed as the "best of my life".
body: Chadwick, a three-time W Series champion and one of the biggest female names in motor racing, drove last season's car at Portimao in Portugal earlier this week.

Chadwick becomes only the second British woman to drive for the Oxfordshire team after Susie Wolff - now the boss of the all-female F1 Academy - in 2015. She completed 32 laps at the Algarve venue which will return to the F1 calendar next year.

"It was a phenomenal day and an incredible experience," said Chadwick. "Few things can prepare you for driving a Formula One car at speed around a track like Portimao, but it was everything I imagined and 10 times more.
"I'm incredibly grateful to Williams for this opportunity. I remember being young and watching Susie Wolff step into a Williams F1 car and how much that inspired my own journey.

articles.title: Drinking at football matches - would fans welcome it?
articles.summary: Andy Burnham has long championed a repeal of the ban which prevents football supporters from drinking alcohol in the view of the pitch. But do fans even want it?
body: When UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham embarked on his trip to the United Nations in New York, he might not have been expecting a question about football fans drinking alcohol in grounds.
Burnham firmly believes the law that prevents supporters from having a beer at their seat during a match is outdated.
It's a position the Everton supporter has long held, and when asked was happy to reaffirm.
"I do believe there is a case to remove that discrimination," said Burnham, who feels football fans are singled out compared to those of other sports and events.

articles.title: Ex-Welsh first minister Jones joins Scarlets board
articles.summary: Former Welsh first minister Carwyn Jones is to join Scarlets' board during a season in which their long-term future is under threat. Jones served as Wales' top politician between 2009 and 2018 and has since become a peer with the title Lord Jones of Penybont.
body: Born in Swansea, Jones attended Aberystwyth University, where he played rugby, before serving as a member of the Senedd for Bridgend for more than 20 years.
Under Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) plans, Scarlets and Swansea-based Ospreys are rivals to remain as one of a three-team professional tier in Wales beyond 2028.

Jones said: "I believe Welsh rugby needs four professional teams. The proposal to leave west Wales with one licence puts two clubs with proud histories and important contributions in an impossible position.
"The west must stand together to secure the future of both of its teams."

Joshua comes into the fight on the back of a major scare during his July victory over Kristian Prenga, with the 36-year-old knocked down twice in the opening round before stopping his unheralded opponent in the second.
The fight was Joshua's first since he survived a December 2025 car crash that claimed the lives of his close friends Sina Ghami and Latif 'Latz' Adodele.
Former cruiserweight world champion Nelson told Sky Sports News: "Well mentally, remember almost a year ago, AJ was involved in a horrific accident.

articles.title: Brewers' Rookie Pitcher Ties MLB Record In Final Regular Season Start
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers beat the Philadelphia Phillies on Wednesday night, and starting pitcher Logan Henderson tied an MLB record. Henderson made his debut last season, but only made five starts. His rookie status is intact through this season, and he is up to 23 career starts.
body: Misiorowski has gotten all of the headlines, but Henderson has been just as good. He has a 2.47 ERA through 18 starts this year. After going five innings and allowing just one earned run, Henderson ried Zac Gallen 's MLB record of starts to start a career allowing three earned runs or fewer.

That's right, Henderson has never made a start in which he allowed more than three earned run. He has allowed exactly three earned runs only three times in his career. He has allowed one or fewer run in 13 of his first 23 starts.

articles.title: 'Pretty pants!' - Norris rules McLaren out of Baku pole fight
articles.summary: Lando Norris says McLaren's pace in Thursday's practice sessions at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix was "pretty pants" and is not expecting to contend for pole position.
body: Norris was 1.5 seconds slower than pace-setter George Russell in second practice with the slow-speed 90-degree corners seemingly not suiting McLaren's car.
McLaren have brought a major upgrade package to the car in Baku, including new sidepods, engine cover, diffuser and floor edge but the new parts have not instantly given them more performance.

"We are miles off. We are up there relative and in the position we expect to be in but we are 1.5 seconds off the pace. Pretty pants," said Norris, who is 106 points behind championship leader Kimi Antonelli with nine rounds to go.

Asked if McLaren can close their practice deficit to Mercedes, he added: "I hope so. I have no idea. We will see what work we can do tonight. The car doesn't feel that bad, so it's a little knife in the heart when you see how far off you are.

articles.title: Fury vs Joshua: Both fighters to earn British record paydays
articles.summary: Frank Warren has revealed that Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua will each earn more than any British fighter has previously been paid for a single bout when they finally meet on December 11.
body: The long-awaited all-British heavyweight showdown was finally confirmed on Thursday as the date and venue - Cardiff's Principality Stadium - were announced by the fight's promoters.
Despite both fighters having signed to face each other, the fight was in major doubt amid a dispute over the location before Cardiff was agreed upon as the host.
Warren, Fury's long-time promoter, told Sky Sports News: "They're getting paid more than any British fighter has earned in a fight ever.
"That's why no one could walk away from it because of the amount of money involved. From Tyson's position he really, really wants this fight.
